# Odysseús, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Odysseús** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

The Odyssey is his biography, but his story begins in the Iliad and ends in prophecy. He is the one hero whose full arc — war, wandering, homecoming — the tradition preserves entire. Ten years of force had not taken Troy; Odysseús took it in a night by craft.  The horse, built by Epeios with Athena's help, carried the pick of the Achaeans within the walls as a pretended offering, and the Odyssey remembers it as his design.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Odysseús
- **ASCII form:** odysseus
- **Meaning:** "Hated, painful"
- **Domain of influence:** Cunning, Journey
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ὀδυσσεύς
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 173 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ὀδυσσεύς**. On the evidence, it means "Hated, painful".

Strip **Odysseús** to *odysseus* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **u → ú** — Acute on u: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Odysseús** lives at [/sites/odysseus/](/sites/odysseus/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/odysseus/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/odysseus/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/odysseus/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Odysseús** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** — The sea-crossing hero; the archetype of the long voyage home.
- **Writing, Publishing & Media** — The Odyssey is the foundational travel narrative of the West.
- **Travel, Tourism & Place Branding** — The original odyssey — the journey as transformation.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
